What’s in it for you?
Ready to make a serious impact? Millions of people already rely on Calendly, and we’re still in the midst of exciting product growth — it’s a fantastic time to join us. Everything you’ll work on here will accelerate your career to the next level. If you want to learn, grow, and do the best work of your life alongside the best people you’ve ever worked with, then we hope you’ll consider allowing Calendly to be a part of your professional journey.
About the team & opportunity
Millions of people use Calendly to book meetings, and most of that happens on public booking pages where anyone with a link can schedule time. That openness is what makes Calendly easy to use, and it’s also what makes it a target. The Trust & Safety team keeps Calendly safe without slowing anyone down.
We protect everyone who interacts with Calendly: the hosts who share their links, the invitees who book with them, and the email and SMS providers and partners who rely on us to send responsibly. Our work covers three areas: preventing and responding to abuse, protecting the deliverability and compliance of the messages Calendly sends, and keeping messaging costs predictable as the platform grows.
Most of our problems are adversarial. We often can’t rely on knowing who someone is, so we judge behavior, patterns, and content instead. Attackers change tactics all the time, so we build signals that last from one attack to the next. And we take false positives seriously, because blocking a real customer costs more than letting a spammer through. Engineers work closely with our Trust & Safety Operations team, who see abuse first and shape what we build.
In this role, you will report to the Engineering Manager for the Trust & Safety team.
A day in the life of a Full Stack Engineer at Calendly
On a typical day, you will be working on:
Building and improving the systems that detect and stop abuse across sign-up, booking, and messaging, such as spam, phishing, bots, and fraudulent SMS traffic.
Improving the reliability, deliverability, and compliance of the email and SMS notifications Calendly sends.
Shipping new detection carefully: measuring how it performs on real traffic before it acts on accounts, and weighing false positives against false negatives.
Responding to active abuse, including during on-call, by stopping the damage fast, then replacing quick fixes with durable ones.
Building tools that help our Trust & Safety Operations team review accounts faster and understand why the system took each action.
Partnering with Product, Operations, and Data to define requirements and measure the impact of what we ship.
Working with other product teams to add protections to the flows they own.
Reviewing implementation plans and pull requests, and sharing what you learn with the team.
What do we need from you?
3+ years of professional software development experience at a SaaS or technology company, including building and running production systems.
Strong backend skills: building services, APIs, and data-heavy workflows in a service-oriented architecture.
Experience with Rails, Node/TypeScript, Go, or a comparable language or framework, and a willingness to work across more than one.
Comfort with relational databases and SQL, and with using data to check whether a change actually worked.
An analytical, curious mindset: you think about how a system could be misused, not only how it’s supposed to be used.
Good judgment about trade-offs, such as stopping bad actors without adding friction for real customers.
A commitment to clean, reliable, maintainable code, thoughtful testing, and shipping in small increments.
Clear communication with engineers and non-engineers alike, including Operations and Support partners.
Comfort and skill with AI tools in your engineering work, including reviewing their output critically.
Availability to take part in an on-call rotation for critical services.
Authorized to work lawfully in the United States of America as Calendly does not engage in immigration sponsorship at this time.
Nice to have
Experience in trust and safety, fraud, spam, or abuse prevention.
Experience with email or SMS delivery, such as deliverability, sender reputation, or messaging compliance.
Experience with bot protection, rate limiting, or third-party risk and verification services.
Experience building rules engines, risk scoring, or ML-backed decisions in production.
Experience using LLMs to classify or moderate user-generated content.
Experience with GCP, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, or Redis.

Why AssemblyAI

AssemblyAI builds the best-in-class Voice AI models powering the next generation of voice applications. Our models serve 600M+ inference calls monthly, process 1M+ hours of audio daily, and power 2 billion+ end-user experiences. The Voice AI space is at an inflection point; we’re looking for folks truly excited to join a small team and help define the future of the industry.

We are one of the most capital-efficient AI companies on the planet - with under 100 people generating roughly $600K ARR per employee, we sit among the top 5 most revenue-dense teams within the fastest-growing AI companies today. That's not an accident; it's a deliberate choice to stay lean, move fast, and give every person on the team outsized ownership and impact. With thousands of customers including Granola, Fireflies, Figure AI, and CallRail, the company has real scale - processing over 2 million hours of audio daily and handling more than 1 million API calls every day. This is a rare growth-stage opportunity where the business is proven and the trajectory is steep, but the team is still small enough that your fingerprints are on everything.

If you've ever felt buried under layers of bureaucracy, starved of real ownership, or frustrated watching your work disappear into a slow-moving org, AssemblyAI is built differently. The company operates as a true meritocracy, with no heavy planning or approval processes and no gatekeeping on the tools or information you need. For anyone who genuinely cares about voice AI, not as a trend to chase, but as a technology to build, this is the place where the most interesting problems at the most interesting scale are being solved by a team small enough that you'll actually know everyone's name.

We’re committed to creating a space where our employees can bring their full selves to work and have equal opportunity to succeed. No matter your race, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, origin, ability, age, veteran status, if joining this mission speaks to you, we encourage you to apply!

About the role:

More and more developers don't read our docs or click through our dashboard. Their coding agent does. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and others are now how a big share of engineers discover, integrate and debug AssemblyAI. We've spent years polishing the human experience. The agent experience (AX) is newer, growing fast, and almost untouched.

That's the job. You'll own how AI agents build with AssemblyAI: the skills, prompts, MCP server, code samples, docs and integrations an agent reads and runs when a developer says "add transcription to my app." Your north star is simple: an agent should go from zero to a working, production-grade AssemblyAI integration on the first try.

You'll work closely with senior engineers on our Product Engineering team, with real ownership from day one and room to grow into leading AX as the area scales.

What You’ll Do:

- Drive the agent experience. Treat coding agents as a first-class user of AssemblyAI, alongside the humans who use our dashboard and Playground.

- Build and maintain agent skills. Ship skills for our core products (Speech-to-Text, Real-time, Dictation, Voice Agents, TTS, LLM Gateway) that teach agents how to integrate us correctly.

- Build on our MCP server and agent integrations. Extend the AssemblyAI MCP server, help ship agent and MCP auth (OAuth and API keys), and make it easy to plug into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and whatever comes next.

- Make our docs and code samples agent-ready. Own llms.txt, machine-readable docs, quickstarts and SDK examples so agents pick the right API, parameters and patterns the first time.

- Tune the prompts and instructions behind our product. Improve the system prompts, tool definitions and agent instructions that power our in-dashboard agent and onboarding flows.

- Measure it. Build evals and benchmarks that run real coding agents against real integration tasks. Track success rate, time to first working call, and activation from agent-driven signups.

- Help us scale the playbook. Start with one product and then roll what works across every product.

- Use AI tools as a core part of how you work, and help the rest of engineering build faster with agents.

What You’ll Need:

- 2+ years of professional software engineering experience, with solid full-stack fundamentals (Javascript and/or Python).

- Daily, hands-on use of coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex, and real curiosity about what makes them succeed or fail.

- Some hands-on experience writing prompts, skills, tool definitions or agent instructions, at work or side projects, and an interest in measuring them with evals rather than vibes.

- Product sense for developer-facing work. You care whether the developer, or their agent, actually gets to a working integration.

- Clear technical writing. Much of this role is writing that agents and humans both read.

- Comfort with ambiguity and a bias to ship. AX is a new discipline, and you'll learn it and help define it alongside us.

Nice to Have:

- Working knowledge of MCP, LLM tool calling, and how agents read docs and APIs.

- You've built or contributed to an MCP server, agent skill library, or coding agent plugin.

- Developer relations, docs engineering, or SDK experience at an API-first company.

- Experience with Voice AI, speech-to-text, or LLM APIs.

- You've shipped something that agents use in the wild, and can show us the before and after.
